title: Vaccine effectiveness evaluation across diverse populations
bottleneck: Vaccine trials and real-world effectiveness studies concentrate in wealthy countries, leaving almost no data on how vaccines perform in low-income settings with different nutrition, co-infections, and age structures. Fragmented, underreported surveillance systems make it impossible to know whether a vaccine works equally well everywhere.
why_it_blocks: Global vaccination strategy is built on effectiveness data from unrepresentative populations. If vaccines underperform where disease burden is highest, schedules and formulations are miscalibrated worldwide.
current_state: Post-COVID analyses documented the evaluation gap explicitly. Standardized effectiveness surveillance in low-income settings remains rare, and immunosenescence further complicates extrapolation to elderly populations. Immunosenescence means elderly vaccine responses differ systematically from trial populations, yet age-stratified effectiveness data are rarely collected, leaving dosing for the oldest old essentially empirical.
